description: Collapsed 6-category classification taxonomy for the SIF precursor detection model, with the original 11 fine-grained sub-tags nested underneath for explainability/display. Collapsing from 11 to 6 top-level classes addresses training-data sparsity (12 source cases cannot reliably support 11 independent classes) while preserving all original evidence via sub-tags.
source_corpus: 12 OISD case studies (see /mnt/user-data/outputs/training_data.csv for the underlying 75 precursor-text rows)

Case 1.title: Fatal accident during laying down of Drill Pipe on Catwalk through V-door

Case 2.title: Fatal Accident at Workover Rig (Monkey board fall)

Case 6.title: Fatal accident caused by tubing drop after elevator unlatched at monkey board

Case 7.title: Man Overboard (MOB) at offshore unmanned platform

Case 8.title: Fatal Accident during dismantling of Drilling Rig

Case 9.title: Gas blowout incident at Workover Rig

Case 10.title: Oil Pipeline leakage Incident in an Offshore Pipeline

Case 11.title: Fatal incident in Pipeline ROW during excavation for TLP cable repair

Case 12.title: Pipeline failure incidents due to heavy rainfall/flash floods (Monsoon 2025)

top_level_classes.description: Personnel operating without adequate hands-on training, valid/verifiable certification, induction on transfer, or demonstrated competency matching their certified level.

sub_tags.description: Missing hands-on training, unapproved/unverifiable certifications, or certified competency not matching demonstrated knowledge.

supporting_cases.evidence: Victim recently approved as Topman but had received no hands-on training on safety gear, hazard spotting, or emergency response.
No structured training module existed for electrical crew on AHU/compressor maintenance and troubleshooting.
All workers performing high-pressure gasket replacement were in the 'unskilled' category.
Key personnel held valid well control certificates, but demonstrated knowledge did not match the certificate level; recently transferred managers had no induction/orientation.
BOSIET training undertaken by contractual employees was not approved by the Directorate General of Shipping (DGS).
Crew members other than the Driller had no prior experience with the rig's dismantling procedure; structured safety training was not consistently conducted.

top_level_classes.description: Absent, disengaged, or uncoordinated supervisory oversight, and failures in transferring critical operational status information between crew members or roles during active tasks.

sub_tags.description: No mentor/supervisor assigned, or all key supervisory personnel simultaneously absent during a critical or high-risk job.

supporting_cases.evidence: OIM and authorized representatives failed to review and verify Category III inspection reports, allowing critical deficiencies to go unnoticed.
No mentor or supervisor was assigned to provide on-the-job guidance to the newly approved topman.
Deficient leadership and lack of supervision over a highly pressurized gasket-replacement activity.
Installation Manager, HSE Engineer, Rig Superintendent, Rig Manager, and HSE Advisor were ALL absent from the site simultaneously during the critical job.
Deep excavation in restricted conditions was carried out as an entirely unsupervised activity.

sub_tags.description: Critical operational status not relayed between crew roles (floor-to-topman, signalman-to-crane-operator, contractor-to-owner), leading to premature or uncoordinated actions.

supporting_cases.evidence: Placement of the pin end on the incline ramp at the V-door was not conveyed to the topman, who unlatched the elevator while unaware of rig floor activity.
Communication gap between signalman and crane operator regarding sling tensioning; each gave a conflicting account of whether a signal was given.

Mainline contractor executed mechanized excavation without informing the pipeline owner; permit system failed to record the authorized supervisor's name; no post-incident coordination with local police.

top_level_classes.description: Skipped or superficial OEM/statutory inspections, missing calibration/test records, non-standard component substitution, and resulting undetected mechanical or structural degradation.

sub_tags.description: OEM-recommended inspections skipped or incomplete; non-standard components used in place of specified parts; calibration/integrity testing records missing.

supporting_cases.evidence: No evidence of Category II inspection; Category III reports missing core dimensional checks; OEM latch pin replaced with an undersized, loose 6mm cotter pin.
No written OEM monthly inspection guidelines; no calibration records for low/high-pressure switches.
Inadequate daily checklist verification of the twin stop device, allowing it to remain bypassed/unset.
Railings/handrails attached by non-standard method, with rusted or cracked mounting bases.
No periodic inspection report was available for the ratchet boomer, which had pre-existing damage.
Pigging and inline inspection were never conducted since commissioning due to wax buildup.

sub_tags.description: Sudden or progressive physical/structural failure of load-bearing or safety-critical hardware, often the direct trigger event following an undetected maintenance gap.

supporting_cases.evidence: Elevator unlatched due to a rusted, broken latch spring combined with an undersized, loose cotter pin.
Dislodgement/snapping of HVAC compressor terminals sprayed compressor oil onto live terminals, causing an explosion.
Mezzanine deck handrail failed structurally under the worker's weight due to weak base material (rusted weld / cracked composite).
Ratchet boomer's hook section detached during loosening, due to excessive tension or pre-existing damage.

top_level_classes.description: Work executed without required Work Permit/JSA/Toolbox Talk coverage, planning that ignores available historical/offset data, known unsafe conditions tolerated without correction, and identified corrective actions delayed past a reasonable window.

sub_tags.sub_tag_name: Flawed Risk Assessment and Operational Planning
sub_tags.description: Job Safety Analysis (JSA) or well/operational plans omit known hazards, ignore offset-well or historical data, or the job proceeds outside a validated safe operating envelope (e.g. pressure limits).

supporting_cases.evidence: Oil-contaminated, slippery surfaces were not identified or addressed in the JSA or Toolbox Talk.
Inadequate hazard identification/risk assessment; compressor explosion hazard not included in the rig risk register.
Work on a pressurized flange performed without a Work Permit, JSA, or Toolbox Talk.
Well planning predicted an oil-bearing formation and omitted a Blind Shear Ram, ignoring offset-well and prior-workover gas-influx data.
JSA did not include steps for un-securing the travelling block or for safe harness anchoring locations.
Workover plan assumed oil sand per a GTO while ignoring gas shows seen during actual drilling and at a reference offset well.
Pipeline continued running above safe operating pressure for over a year after an MTM survey flagged ERF>1 anomalies.
Excavation to 3.7m depth carried out without considering/mitigating hazards from nearby buildings, deep-rooted trees, and pipeline proximity.
Assumptions regarding parallel-pipeline washout safety were flawed; open-cut river crossings selected without designing for adequate trench depth or pipe thickness once HDD proved unfeasible.

sub_tags.sub_tag_name: Weak Safety Culture and Non-Adherence to Procedures
sub_tags.description: Hazard-reporting systems treated as a formality, obvious hazards tolerated without action, personal devices used during critical operations, or task-specific PPE/procedure bypassed by habit.

supporting_cases.evidence: Unsafe rig conditions went unreported by the crew; reporting procedure treated as a mere formality rather than adopted with genuine intent.
Topman failed to engage full-body harness double hooks to the ladder; climbing conducted simultaneously with tubing pull-out.
Systemic non-adherence to Permit-to-Work protocols, JSAs, and face/eye protective gear.
Rig crew used mobile phones on-duty; a non-standard rope pull was used to unlatch the elevator instead of the approved method.
Personnel chose not to wear mandatory work vests/lifejackets while staying on the unmanned platform.

sub_tags.description: A permanent engineering fix (realignment, pressure de-rating, HDD reroute) is identified and planned, but administrative/logistical delay in execution leaves the known risk live until failure occurs.

supporting_cases.evidence: Management did not execute immediate pressure reduction or corrective actions despite MTM survey identifying extreme anomalies and predicted failure risk.
Longer-length HDD realignment planned after known riverbank erosion, but execution delay left the pipeline operating over the vulnerable zone until failure.

top_level_classes.description: A designated engineered safety barrier (BOP shear ram, trip tank + alarm, interlock, fire water pump, fixed suppression system) is either absent from the equipment configuration or present but non-functional/bypassed at the time of the incident.

sub_tags.sub_tag_name: Defunct or Absent Critical Safety Devices
sub_tags.description: Primary or secondary engineered safety barrier missing from design/configuration, or present but disabled/non-functional at time of incident.

supporting_cases.evidence: Fixed fire suppression system was absent from the workshop area, hampering firefighting in poor visibility.
BOP stack lacked a Blind Shear Ram; trip tank not connected, its level alarm defunct; no active well monitoring; blind ram incorrectly closed on wireline.
Twin stop device failed to function/engage during the runaway descent of the travelling block, having been bypassed or left unset.
BOP stack lacked a blind shear ram; trip tank kept isolated during perforation; fire water pump completely missing from site.
Safety instrumentation and interlocks meant to trip crude oil pumps on abrupt pressure drop malfunctioned during the leak.

top_level_classes.description: External environmental forces (weather, waterway dynamics) or uncontrolled physical conditions in the immediate workspace (obstructions, spillage, combustible storage) that independently elevate risk regardless of procedural compliance.

sub_tags.description: Weather or waterway-driven forces (monsoon, flooding, riverbank erosion/meandering) directly cause or worsen the incident, or hamper emergency response.

supporting_cases.evidence: Monsoon weather conditions directly hindered search-and-rescue (SAR) operations for the missing overboard worker.
Heavy downpours, cloudbursts, and flash floods drove river-path meandering and riverbed erosion, exerting hydrodynamic stress on exposed pipelines.

sub_tags.description: Physical blockage of a climbing/operational path, materials obstructing visibility or access, spillage creating slip hazards, or combustible material stored in an active work area.

supporting_cases.evidence: Materials placed on the rig floor obstructed the tugger operator's line of sight.
Standpipe gooseneck and Kelly hose obstructed the monkey ladder; crude oil spillage from wet pull-out made the derrick floor and ladder slippery.
Combustible glass wool duct insulation present; an overhead platform was used to store combustible mechanical spares and filters.

coverage_summary.note: Case coverage counts per class reflect unique cases (a case may appear under multiple sub-tags if it exhibits more than one precursor type, which is expected and realistic for multi-causal incidents).
